newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares recover, back in 1,120-1,140 range.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares recover, back in 1,120-1,140 range.

text.p: Austrian shares rebounded 1.26 percent on Monday and traders said the market looked to have overcome last Friday's sharp fall and resumed its upward march.
The ATX shares of 21 blue-chip shares closed 14.01 points up at 1,122.41 -- above the technically signficant 1,120 points level and back in the 1,120-1,140 points trading range established last week.
Overall 19 shares ended higher and two lower. December ATX futures stood 13.0 points up at 1,116.0.
"It's back to business as usual," said a trader.
"(U.S. Federal Reserve chief Alan) Greenspan took the euphoria out of the market on Friday, but in technical terms it was just a hiccup. Prices have recovered very quickly," said a second trader.
Greenspan triggered a Europe-wide sell-off on Friday when he said gains on Wall Street may be overdone.
Chip producer Austria Mikro Systeme, which bore the brunt of Friday's fall, was the day's biggest gainer. It climbed 4.18 percent, or 33 schillings, to 823 schillings.
Luxiery hosiery maker Wolford also advanced, firming 32 schillings to 1,260 ahead of half-year earnings due next Monday.
EA-Generali was the leading decliner, easing 1.09 percent, or 40 schillings, to 3,640 schillings.
Steelmaker VA Stahl, which earlier reported lower nine-month earnings but forecast a slight market upturn in the fourth quarter, gained 8.8 schillings to 398.8.
Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien, which said it would recommend a higher 1996 dividend payment, rose 10 schillings to 522.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index was 2.98 points up at 425.69. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
